quest.title: Annals of the Scarlet Sands
quest.description: During your investigation, you accidentally stumbled upon Dunyarzad's father's name. After discussing the matter with Dehya, she decides that Dunyarzad should be informed of all that has transpired...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Mora x34075, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

talks.objective: Return to Sumeru City to talk to Dunyarzad

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: We're back, my lady.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back a lot sooner than I expected! You mustn't have run into any trouble, then. Well, how did it go? What did you come up with?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Actually, we are still investigating. It's just that... we've discovered something strange.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I see... the clues you found have led you back here in the city?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Something like that, yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: You all look a little dispirited. Whatever you found must not have been very encouraging after all.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Why don't you discuss it with me? Maybe I'll be able to say something to cheer you up.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It's okay, my lady, it's not so much about me being upset with my father or anything like that... Ugh, how should I put this...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: So something IS wrong. Even the Traveler and Paimon have been uncharacteristically quiet...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: On any other day, Paimon would have already waved to me with a smile and shouted "Dunyarzad, we're baaaack!"

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: So tell me, what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, w—well...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My lady, please prepare yourself for what we're going to tell you next. It concerns the master...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: The master... You mean my father?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Okay, I understand. Don't worry about me, I'll listen as attentively as I can.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Dehya manages to explain the results of the investigation to Dunyarzad.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: My father... has been supplying goods to Dakan Al-Ahmar?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yeah. It makes as little sense to us as it does to you.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I've never doubted the master's integrity, so I'm having a real hard time rationalizing how he could ever support an infamous brigade like them.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Maybe he's not actually aware of the full story, and just stumbled into the deal by accident...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That feels unlikely, though.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I can't help but agree with the Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean you feel the same way, Dunyarzad?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Thank you for sharing all this information with me.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Since you've told me everything you know... I should also tell you about some doubts that I've been harboring for quite a while.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: In the past, I thought that my father hired a bodyguard for me so that I wouldn't run away and get lost.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: However, there are plenty of capable mercenaries in the Corps of Thirty. Why did my father go out of his way to hire Dehya?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ah, about that... well, the Homayanis really needed bodyguards, so they reached out to the Blazing Beasts.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Later, the master told me that I was one of the best mercenaries he'd ever seen, and that I should stick around to become one of his bodyguards.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: He offered me a pile of Mora, so I just signed on...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Well, but that didn't really answer my question. Just think about it... why did my father specifically reach out to the Blazing Beasts?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Err, maybe the Corps of Thirty just didn't have anyone available? Or maybe someone recommended us? I've never given it too much thought...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...I think I get what you're saying. You think none of this was a coincidence.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Precisely. At first glance, nothing seems strange or out of place, but there are many parts of the story that don't actually make any sense.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: If my father had always been in contact with Dakan Al-Ahmar... then it would make sense for him to bring Dehya into our house.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean, the goal all along was to get Dehya to be your bodyguard?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: No no no, that's too much of a stretch. I cut all my ties with my father a long time ago. He has no control over my life anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: But that still doesn't rule out the possibility that your father has still been trying to influence your life without you knowing.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So... the master was not likely an innocent victim in all of this?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's what things are looking like at this point.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry we put all this on you so suddenly, Dunyarzad...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: It's okay, Paimon. I should actually be thanking you.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Regardless of his reasons, if my father has truly been funding a violent group of mercenaries, then it's my duty to bring him back to reason.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But is that... really the right thing to do?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My father has committed many atrocities, and deserves all the punishment that he has coming to him. I have zero sympathy for him. You may call me an ungrateful child, but my feelings will remain the same.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: However... the Homayani family has treated me with nothing but generosity and kindness.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If we decide to investigate this further, we could end up implicating the entire Homayani family. I would be biting the hand that's fed me over all these years...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: It's alright, Dehya. If anyone were to ask, you could always just say that I'm the one who instructed you to get to the bottom of this.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You don't have to do that, my lady. I'm not conflicted because I'm afraid of taking responsibility... Besides, you're the one we should all be worried about right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's still too early to give up hope! What was that thing about friendship again...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: True friendship is built on trust.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, yeah, trust! You said that yourself, Dehya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Besides, there's no point on getting all riled up before we've even confirmed all the facts!

choices.text: If your trust hasn't been misplaced...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Thank you, everyone. That makes a lot of sense. I guess I should always remember the trust that I've placed in people.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: In which case... my lady, could you ask the master to come out and have a chat with us?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Sure thing. I also hope he'll be able to give us a logical explanation. Let's meet at the usual place, then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The... usual place? Ah, right!

choices.text: Then he probably has many conflicting feelings as well.

talks.objective: Wait for Dunyarzad at the usual place

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Thank you for coming, sir.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #Please allow me to introduce these two. This is {NICKNAME}, and next to {M#him}{F#her} is {M#his}{F#her} travel companion, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Ah yes, my daughter has mentioned them from time to time. It's a privilege to finally meet them in person.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: But we may skip all the pleasantries for now, what is the important matter you wished to discuss with me today?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Well, we wanted to bring this transaction record to your attention. There's something on this record that we're all pretty curious about...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Dehya explains the issue to Shahzaman, and admits her doubts to him.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: So that's what you've found, huh... Seems like I can't keep everything from you much longer.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If you wouldn't mind, we'd like an explanation.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Well, it's a long and difficult story, and to be perfectly honest, I'm not sure if I'm doing the right thing.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: What I do know though, Dehya, is that the truth will bring you no solace. If anything, it will likely cause you a great amount of anguish.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Wait... me?

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Yes. I understand perfectly why you came to see me, and I am touched by your collective commitment to do the right thing.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: But knowledge always comes at a price, and sometimes, as they say, ignorance is bliss.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Your father Kusayla and I both believed that.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Of course, you have the right to seek and learn the truth, but I must warn you...

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: That the facts of this matter may reduce everything you've built for yourself into sand blowing in the wind.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: If you must proceed, then Kusayla's heartfelt efforts will also fade into the wind like a fleeting mirage.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: His... heartfelt efforts? I'm sorry sir, but I'm not sure I follow.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I've made it this far in life without a single drop of my father's support.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I have my own ideals and ways of looking at the world, as well as people and causes that I've chosen to cherish and fight for... None of these things have anything to do with him.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I came here today to support you as the head of the Homayani family. No warning will change my stance on that.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: *sigh* I understand. Then let me tell you a little story.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Our family once needed to take a trip to the desert when Dunyarzad was just a baby. Along the way, we were attacked by bandits.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: They had superior numbers, and quickly overpowered our bodyguards. When all seemed lost, a group of passerby Eremites lent us their support.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Those Eremites were Kusayla's brigade, Dakan Al-Ahmar.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Kusayla's men told me that the attackers were Eremite mercenaries just like themselves. I was shocked. Why would Dakan Al-Ahmar go so far to save us, and not spare the fellow Eremites?

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Kusayla was grinning and walked over to play with baby Dunyarzad. She was startled by his unfamiliar face and nearly started crying.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Really? I... never knew...

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: He said that he had no particular reason to help us. He just took pity on us because he had a daughter about the same age.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: We started talking about our children, and I sensed that he was a devoted father.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: To repay his kindness, I hired his brigade to help out at our estate for a time, and offered everyone generous remuneration.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So that's what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: It was many years before I saw him again. I almost didn't recognize him the next time he came knocking on my door.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: The man I knew to be strong and healthy had been reduced to a... shell of himself. He couldn't even walk anymore without his cane.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So what happened to him? He was perfectly fine when I left the brigade...

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: I'm not too sure myself. The only thing that didn't change was his cheery disposition. He said there was absolutely nothing to worry about and that he had gotten into a fight, that was all.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: He then suddenly asked me if Dunyarzad, now that she had grown, would need a bodyguard of her own.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: At the time, Dunyarzad was going through a particularly severe bout of her Eleazar. There was no need for her to have a bodyguard when she could barely leave the house...

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: But he kept coming back to the topic... "C'mon, it never hurts to be safe." "How do you know a bodyguard won't come in handy one day?"

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: I was completely lost at first, until he recommended the "Blazing Beasts," and in particular, a mercenary named Dehya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So he was the one who recommended Dehya to you!

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Indeed. He didn't say it out loud, but it was clear that he saw Deshret's Relics as an evil group who would eventually corrupt every member in their ranks.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: He was already beyond redemption, but he hoped that he would be able to detach his daughter from the vicious world of mercenary life.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: If Dehya could stay in my house and keep working as a bodyguard, then gradually her affinity for the desert would decrease, and she'd be able to leave her previous life behind.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: And that's why you offered her such generous compensation?

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Yes, but not just because of that. From the moment that he asked me for that favor, I also began to see Dehya as my own daughter.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: And that's also why I tried to persuade you to stay when you asked for permission to leave. I was willing to spend however much it took...

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Kusayla saved my daughter and me all those years ago in the desert. I could never refuse him entrusting his daughter to me.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ugh, he was always like that... Acting like he's oh-so-smart and self-righteous...

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Kusayla said that he'd reimburse me for a portion of Dehya's fees. I refused to take any Mora from him, but he'd always send me funds anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: Eventually, I just accepted them as a token of his gratitude. That went on for a while, until I received another letter from him a few years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: The letter contained a request to help him buy food, weapons, medicine, and even explosive materials.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, isn't that around the time that Dakan Al-Ahmar started becoming more aggressive?

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: That's right. When I started to hear some nasty rumors, I became wary, and wanted to meet him face-to-face to discuss things.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: But by then, he was no longer receptive to my requests to talk. If I had to guess... it's probably because he doesn't want to put Dehya at risk.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But by that same token, he should have also stopped asking you for materials.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: That thought occurred to me as well. I figured that he probably came to me for help because he had nobody else to turn to.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: After some deliberation, I decided to send him some food and medicine. I turned down all his requests for explosives and weaponry.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: I am aware that even such a reduced gesture of support could lead to others coming to harm, but I could not simply reject his plea for help.

dialogues.speaker: Shahzaman
dialogues.text: In the end, it probably was the wrong decision. I plugged my ears to the rumors and just chose the solution that made me feel least guilty about myself.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...If you can, please tell me where he is now.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: None of the things he's doing right now make any sense if he's just trying to keep me from getting tangled up in his world...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If all he wants to do is steer clear of me, then maybe he shouldn't have brought me into this world in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, Dehya, please don't feel that way...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm just angry because I can't wrap my head around any of his actions.

choices.text: Maybe there's another way of looking at all of this...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Another way? I dunno... I knew him, and he was nothing more than a childish brute. I can't understand what's going through his head.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But I guess you do have a point... We haven't uncovered the whole truth yet. We still need to figure out his exact actions and reasoning for these last few years.

response.speaker: Shahzaman
response.text: I'll do my best to help. Of course, anything between the two of you would need to be resolved between you and him alone.

response.speaker: Shahzaman
response.text: I don't know Kusayla's exact whereabouts. Outside of supplying his brigade with some goods, I tried my best to avoid getting involved any further with him.

response.speaker: Shahzaman
response.text: However, there's a man on the list named <color=#00E1FFFF>Jawad</color>. He used to be a mercenary in the desert, and is now a member of the Corps of Thirty.

response.speaker: Shahzaman
response.text: He's responsible for supplying weapons and liaising with Dakan Al-Ahmar's merchant caravan. I think he should know Kusayla's whereabouts.

response.speaker: Shahzaman
response.text: I've heard that he likes to have a few drinks alone and enjoy the cool wind at <color=#00E1FFFF>night</color> outside of the <color=#00E1FFFF>tavern</color>. Maybe you'll be able to find him there.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Understood, thank you sir. Then I guess this is bye for now, unless...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I'll stay and be with my father here... To be honest, I'm still a little dazed, and haven't finished processing everything quite yet.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: My father has indeed done something wrong, but if I think about it, I'm also not sure if there was a right way to handle this problem.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I feel like... our only course of action is to turn everything we know over to the Corps of Thirty, and let them render judgment...

response.speaker: Shahzaman
response.text: Yes. I am prepared to accept whatever verdict they choose.

response.speaker: Shahzaman
response.text: It's time to face my mistakes...

choices.text: Can you try to believe in him... just one more time?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I don't know, I really don't know... I don't think I can do it.

talks.objective: Go look for <color=#00E1FFFF>Jawad</color> outside the tavern <color=#00E1FFFF>at night</color>

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: Huh? Who are you guys?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I know what you've been up to. Smuggling weapons to violent brigades in the desert while working for the Corps? Pretty bold if you ask me.

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: Shh, keep your voice down! How do you know all that!?

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: Come with me, we should take this elsewhere. I'll be happy to talk things over once we're somewhere private.

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: This place should do... Alright, back to my question, how did you all know about me?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Don't worry about that for now. You know what kind of punishment you'll face once we report you to the Corps, I assume?

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: Wait wait wait, there's no need to jump the gun! Let's talk this out. What are your terms?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what's in it for you anyway? Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: Uhh... Well, I was a little tight on money at the time, and Kusayla took good care of me in the past...

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: I weighed it in my mind, and I couldn't find a reason to turn the opportunity down. I wouldn't only be helping my benefactor, but I could also make some quick Mora...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Let me tell you how it is. We're investigating Dakan Al-Ahmar, and we're gonna put an end to their operations.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If you provide some help for us, then we might just put in a good word later to reduce the terms of your punishment.

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: Hey, why don't we discuss this a little first? Listen, I made quite a bit of Mora from my last run. Just give me a number and I'm sure we can...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Shut it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My patience is running out. You should know when a mercenary is after something other than money.

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, sheesh. But ya gotta promise you'll put in some nice words for me later.

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: They're always on the move. Here's the spot they were at last time I made my delivery to the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: Feel free to go have a look. I'm just telling you, though, it's not on me if they're not there anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Sure, and then you can forget about any nice words from us.

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: Hey, c'mon! Now you're just being unreasonable!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Really? And how do I know you're not leading us straight into a trap? Don't forget, you're the one with no bargaining chips.

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: Alright, I get it, I get it... Why don't you go take a look, and if they're not there anymore, I'll try to figure out something else for you all.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Now that's more like it. Let's move.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: And as for you... try to stick around the city until we get back. You don't want us to call the folks from the Corps and have them drag you back to the city.

talks.objective: Go to the location of Dakan Al-Ahmar
Go to the location of Dakan Al-Ahmar

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm, seems like we're in luck. That should be their camp right up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Let's go. We'll finally get to the bottom of this ourselves.

talks.objective: Talk to Idrisi and the others

dialogues.speaker: Bashar
dialogues.text: Sh—She's so strong...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Enough fighting. We all know each other, and I don't want to take things too far.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Just bring Kusayla to me! There's no use hiding him anymore!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Did you understand a single word I just said? Or do I need to bash your skull in some more?

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Alright, everyone, let's all just calm down for a second.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Um, Dehya, the boss can't come out and see you anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: He died a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: What...?

dialogues.speaker: Bashar
dialogues.text: Seems like you've been out of the loop for a while. Guess that's for the best, though... at least that's what the old man wanted.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: When did he die? What happened to him?

dialogues.speaker: Tikriti
dialogues.text: A few years ago, Kusayla broke up Dakan Al-Ahmar, and went to the Deshret's Relics headquarters by himself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So is that when you guys started acting up?

dialogues.speaker: Bashar
dialogues.text: We would prefer to call it "taking revenge." Every last person in Deshret's Relics must pay in blood for what they did!

choices.text: So that's why they turned on each other...

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: Let me start from the beginning. Dehya, do you know how the head of the Relics maintained order internally?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Overwhelming strength, and unquestionable authority?

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: Those were a part of it, yes. But just those on their own weren't enough. They had another tool at their disposal. They called it a person's "record."

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: Regardless of whether they joined by their own will or were coerced, every person in Deshret's Relics were forced to leave a record of themselves at headquarters.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: Whether it be their deepest sin, some unforgivable act, or their most immoral exploit, the record served both as a symbol of loyalty and the perfect material for blackmail.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: That's precisely it. Every one of us have a record... me, Bashar, Tikriti, and all the boys who grew up with Dehya and ended up joining our ranks.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: But you, Dehya... you were never asked to provide a record, were you?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I... I never even knew this was a requirement...

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: You were probably the only person in all of Deshret's Relics who didn't know about it.

response.speaker: Bashar
response.text: Ever since you were born, boss had been trying to shield you from this organization's sinister rules.

response.speaker: Bashar
response.text: Not only that, but he also banned all of us from committing any nefarious acts. He said he'd take care of the dues we had to pay regularly to headquarters...

response.speaker: Bashar
response.text: But in the end, he was just an ordinary person. What could he do?

response.speaker: Bashar
response.text: He was forced to go to headquarters again and again to account for missed dues and incomplete records. He'd come up with all kinds of excuses, and get beaten up as a result.

response.speaker: Tikriti
response.text: We all knew he was doing that for you. He wanted to get you out of this world, no matter what it took.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...And that was why he became a shell of himself, and couldn't walk without a cane.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Wait, but that doesn't make any sense. I didn't know about any of this, and I'd never seen him get injured or beaten...

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: Because you were too young at the time. How would you ever tell between wounds from a beating and wounds from battle?

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: When you left home after that final argument with him, he seemed to age by a decade overnight. Even his hair went gray.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: So, even the Blazing Beasts were...

response.speaker: Bashar
response.text: Yep, it was all his doing. Had he not arranged them to come to you, you probably would have been reduced to a pulp before you ever left the desert.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: A few years ago, boss said he needed to make another trip to headquarters. He was already pretty weak then, and we all assumed he was going to get beaten again.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: I suggested that he hand the role of leadership over to me, but he said there was no longer any need, since Dakan Al-Ahmar would soon be no more.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: His words made no sense to me, but that night, we heard that a massive fire tore through headquarters, and razed everyone's "records" to ash.

response.speaker: Tikriti
response.text: Everyone gained their freedom that night. Many members fled... not just from our ranks, but from the other brigades as well.

response.speaker: Tikriti
response.text: But how could we leave with a clear conscience? All of us, who knew exactly what had happened...

response.speaker: Bashar
response.text: The boss can't have just died for nothing! Those heartless jerks at headquarters took him from us!

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: From that point on, the sole purpose of Dakan Al-Ahmar became revenge.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: The big fire that boss started was quite a blow to headquarters' strength. It's given us the opportunity to launch our attack.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: Even though we're outnumbered, we've vowed to see our revenge through to the very end.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But Deshret's Relics haven't been the only victims of your revenge.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: There were people from headquarters who changed their names and went into hiding. Some fled to other brigades, and others escaped to the rainforest.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: But we won't let any of them escape our wrath. They'll all pay for what they've done.

response.speaker: Bashar
response.text: We've suffered plenty of losses as well. To keep going, we need an enormous amount of supplies... from food and medicine to weaponry and explosives.

response.speaker: Bashar
response.text: All we can do is exchange our loot for Mora, and then use that to get supplies.

response.speaker: Bashar
response.text: We forged boss's handwriting and sent out many letters to his former friends. Thankfully, many people were willing to come to our aid.

response.speaker: Bashar
response.text: We were also able to attract many mercenaries who shared our goal. We've endured unspeakable pain to win many impossible battles...

response.speaker: Bashar
response.text: Deshret's Relics have become weaker and weaker, and now... we finally have an opportunity to directly strike their headquarters.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Paimon doesn't know what to say anymore.

choices.text: Responding to violence with more violence will only cause more pain.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: Hah, we do know right from wrong. But we were sinners from the very beginning... We do not deserve the freedom that the boss won for us with his life.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: Boss always loved his old-fashioned hero stories... those tales about sacrificing yourself to save the world.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: We used to always laugh at him for it, but in the end, he really went and lived those stories out himself...

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: As for me, I never considered myself a hero. We're all the lowest of the low. We have no right to even imagine such an existence.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: But maybe those hero stories he liked foreshadowed everything that was to come. The spirit of the hero touched all those he had saved, and more and more people joined his cause...

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: Maybe we were all just acting along with the play in the beginning, but as we acted the parts and recited the lines, we were drawn in, and now we want to see the story through to the end...

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: I'm sorry, Dehya. I know you always found us insufferable ever since you were young. Just think of this as a madman ranting.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I'll go with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Dehya, you want to go with them?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I grew up with these guys, and I know they're not bad people. It's just that some situations get so bad that it's difficult to tell good from evil...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: All I know is that Deshret's Relics must be destroyed.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Furthermore... I want to go see the place for myself. I want to know if my father is still there...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I know you don't want to get involved in this, so there's no need for you to tag along. I can do this on my own.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Paimon feels like we'd only regret it if we don't see this through to the end...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Thank you. We'll be a lot stronger together with you.

response.speaker: Idrisi
response.text: Haha, I bet boss would lose his mind if he ever knew you'd join us at the very last moment like this.

response.speaker: Tikriti
response.text: Considering all the losses and injuries we've sustained... We can't afford to turn down someone as powerful as you.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: He can think whatever he wants...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...But the fact is, I owe him this much.

choices.text: No, I made a promise to Dunyarzad to support you.
Do you have any idea the amount of damage you've done?
Kusayla thought there was no escaping the records.
It was all motivated by revenge...

dialogues.speaker: Jawad
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry, I'm not goin' anywhere...

dialogues.speaker: Observe
dialogues.text: (Sattar is not gravely injured, and will probably wake up soon. It should be okay to leave him here for a little while.)

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm here to see Kusayla. Tell him to get out here!

dialogues.speaker: Tikriti
dialogues.text: Huh? Dehya? Why are you here?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Haven't you all done enough?

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Oh, so are you also here to stop us?

dialogues.speaker: Bashar
dialogues.text: Stay outta this! It's got nothing to do with you!
